title: 3-D shapes
keyIdea: A 3-D shape is a solid you can hold, not a flat drawing. A cube has 6 flat faces that are all the same square; a cuboid is a stretched cube with some long rectangle faces. A sphere, like a ball, is round all over with no flat face. A cylinder, like a tin, has 2 flat circle faces and a curved surface; a cone has 1 flat circle face, a curved surface and a point. A pyramid has flat triangle faces that meet at a point. You cannot see every face at once, so turn a solid to count them.

kid: A solid is a shape you can pick up and hold. A ball, a tin and a box are all solids. A drawing on paper is flat.
Feel a solid. Some parts are flat. We call a flat part a face. Some parts are curved. A curved part can roll.
A cube has 6 flat faces. Each face is a square. You can only see 3 at once, so turn it round to count them all. A pyramid has flat triangle faces that meet at the top.
A ball is a sphere. A tin is a cylinder, with a flat circle at each end. A party hat is a cone. A box can be a cuboid, like a long cube.
adult: Naming solids is in US Common Core K.G.A.1 to K.G.A.3 (describe objects using the names of shapes and tell flat, two-dimensional shapes from solid, three-dimensional ones) and in England's Year 1 programme of study (recognise and name common 3-D shapes, including cuboids and cubes, pyramids and spheres). Year 2 then counts faces, edges and vertices.

Use exact words from the start. A face is a flat surface; a cylinder and a cone also have a curved surface, which is not called a face in Year 2 work. A cube is a special cuboid whose 6 faces are all congruent squares. The flat face of a 3-D shape is a 2-D shape, so a cube's face is a square and a cone's base is a circle.

Common mistakes to watch for: calling a solid by a flat name (a ball is a circle, a dice is a square), mixing up a cube and a cuboid, calling a cone a triangle or a pyramid because it looks triangular from the side, counting only the 3 faces you can see on a cube, and thinking a round solid has no flat face at all.

In the lab your child turns a cube and taps each face to count all 6, taps the flat faces and curved surfaces of a cylinder and a cone, names six solids, picks which solid made a paint print, and matches a tin, a ball, a dice, a cereal box and a party hat to their solids.

familyTip: Go on a solid hunt in the kitchen: find a cylinder (a tin), a cuboid (a cereal box) and a sphere (an orange). Press a flat face of each into a little paint or flour and look at the print. Ask: which one did not make a print, and why?

visual.caption: Does it have a curved surface? Drag each solid, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: turn a cube to count its faces, find flat faces and curved surfaces, name six solids, match paint prints and find solids at home.

practice.prompt: What is a ball called in shape words?
practice.hint: A circle is flat, like a drawing. A ball is round all over and you can hold it.
practice.explain: A ball is a sphere. A sphere is a solid that is round all over and has no flat face.

practice.prompt: A cube has 6 faces. You put a sticker on {n} faces. How many faces have no sticker?
practice.hint: A cube has 6 faces in all. Take away the {n} with a sticker.
practice.explain: 6 faces take away {n} with a sticker leaves {=6-n} faces with no sticker.

practice.prompt: {n} tins stand on a shelf. Each tin is a cylinder with 2 flat faces. How many flat faces in all?
practice.hint: Each tin has a flat circle at the top and one at the bottom. Count in 2s, {n} times.
practice.explain: {n} tins with 2 flat faces each make {=2*n} flat faces.

practice.prompt: Which solid has a flat circle face, a curved surface and a point?
practice.hint: Think of a party hat. What shape is its bottom, and what is at the top?
practice.explain: A cone has 1 flat circle face, 1 curved surface and a point. A pyramid has flat triangle faces, and a cylinder has no point.

pool.prompt: Which solid has 6 faces that are all the same square?
pool.hint: Think of a dice. Are all its faces the same?
pool.explain: A cube has 6 square faces, all the same. A cuboid has some long rectangle faces.

pool.prompt: A tin of beans is like which solid?
pool.hint: A tin has a flat circle at each end and a curved side.
pool.explain: 2 flat circle faces and a curved surface make a cylinder.

pool.prompt: Sam calls a dice a square. What is it really?
pool.hint: A square is flat. A dice is a solid you can hold.
pool.explain: A dice is a cube. Each face of a cube is a square, but the whole solid is a cube.

pool.prompt: How many flat faces does a sphere have?
pool.hint: Is any part of a ball flat?
pool.explain: A sphere is curved all over, so it has no flat face. That is why it rolls every way.

pool.prompt: You press a pyramid's side in paint. What shape is the print?
pool.hint: The sides of a pyramid are flat and meet at a point.
pool.explain: A pyramid's side faces are flat triangles, so the print is a triangle.

pool.prompt: You have {n} cones. Each cone has 1 flat face. How many flat faces in all?
pool.hint: Each cone has just 1 flat circle at the bottom. Count the cones.
pool.explain: 1 flat face on each of {n} cones is {n} flat faces.

pool.prompt: A cereal box is long. Which solid is it like?
pool.hint: Are all its faces the same square, or are some long?
pool.explain: Its faces are rectangles and not all the same, so it is a cuboid, not a cube.

pool.prompt: Which of these is a 3-D shape?
pool.hint: Which one can you pick up and hold?
pool.explain: A cone is a solid. A triangle and a circle are flat 2-D shapes.

pool.prompt: A box holds {b} balls and {t} tins. How many cylinders are in the box?
pool.hint: A ball is a sphere. A tin is a cylinder. Count only the tins.
pool.explain: Only the tins are cylinders, so there are {t}. The {b} balls are spheres.
